author: Paget Kagy | Quantum Queen
transcript: Universe, why is everything getting harder the closer I get? The biggest client just backed out this morning. The investor pulled the funding. The man that I thought I was finally ready to commit to is pulling away. I am this close. Is this even meant for me? Of course it is. Then why is this happening? Let me ask you something, okay? In a basketball game, when is the defense the lightest? On the other side of the basket? Right, and when is it the heaviest? When you're close to the basket. When you're an inch from the rim, body's in front of you, hands in your face, five players headed straight towards you. Okay, that's what's happening to you right now. Oh, far from your goal, there was no resistance because you weren't close enough to be a threat. Now you're a threat, so everything that doesn't want you to score is showing up at once. So it's not the universe punishing me? It's the universe mirroring your own resistance to success. My resistance? Every doubt that's loudest right now, it's yours. Every obstacle feels designed to stop you because it's the version of you that's terrified to win. Oh my gosh. The closer you get to the goal, the more your own internal defenses rise up because some part of you doesn't know who you'll be when you finally have what you want. So what do I do? Walk into the resistance. This isn't proof it's not meant for you. It's proof you're inches from the rim.
title: Resistance Means You're Almost There
one_liner: Increased obstacles near your goal signal internal resistance, not external punishment — you're close to winning.
key_points: Defense gets heaviest when you're closest to the basket — same applies to life goals
External setbacks mirror your own internal fear of success, not the universe blocking you
The louder your doubts, the closer you are to breakthrough
Walk into the resistance instead of retreating from it
